Krapina Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Krapina, Croatia

Not demolished. Krapina, first mentioned in 1193 with a fortress from 1258, developed as a woodworking-craft center after 18th-century earthquake recovery. Jews arrived in the 19th century as members of nearby Varaždin's Jewish community rather than an independent congregation; population never exceeded about 60 (1931), falling to 45 before WWII and just 9 afterward. This cemetery, part of the municipal cemetery, was established in 1890 (nationalized 1958); its ceremonial hall was destroyed roughly 20 years before this survey. Tombstones span 1887 to 1971.
